report:
**Conclusion: The claim is not supported by scientific evidence.**

Multiple large studies and meta-analyses have found no causal relationship between childhood vaccines—or the number of vaccines given—and autism. A 2014 meta-analysis pooling data from over 1.2 million children found no link between MMR, thimerosal-containing vaccines, or cumulative antigen exposure and autism. More than 40 studies involving millions of children have reached the same conclusion. The original 1998 paper that sparked concern was retracted, and subsequent research consistently shows vaccinated and unvaccinated children have the same autism risk. Autism onset timing coincides with vaccine schedules, which can create a false impression of linkage, but the consensus is clear: vaccines do not cause autism.

**Sources:**

- https://www.chop.edu/vaccine-education-center/vaccine-safety/vaccines-and-other-conditions/autism
- https://www.forbes.com/sites/emilywillingham/2014/05/15/vaccines-thimerosal-mmr-mercury-not-associated-with-autism/
- https://www.aap.org/en/news-room/fact-checked/fact-checked-vaccines-safe-and-effect-no-link-to-autism/
